messages:
samir: Heads-up — seeing a cluster-wide scheduling blip in eu-west-1. Lots of GPU pods Pending with Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu even though node GPU utilization is low. Filing here before paging oncall.
lee: which nodepool? dedicated-gpu or spot-gpu?
samir: dedicated-gpu nodepool-rtx6000. Affected pods are mixed: some cuda-based training jobs (1 gpu), some small preprocessing jobs that request 0.25 gpu (weird). Example error from describe:

```
Events:
  Type     Reason         Age   From               Message
  ----     ------         ----  ----               -------
  Warning  FailedScheduling  2m    default-scheduler  0/10 nodes are available: 10 Insufficient nvidia.com/gpu.
```

But `nvidia-smi` on nodes shows free GPU memory and no processes.
anya: fractional requests (0.25) shouldn't be allowed by device plugin — are we using a custom device plugin that supports fractional allocation?
maria: we rolled out multi-instance GPU plugin (MIG-like) for rtx6000 last week. It exposes shared resources as "gpu-shares" with capacity math on CRI. Could be mismatch in capacity accounting.
samir: cluster-autoscaler also didn't add nodes. CA logs show it considered nodes not needed because pods request "nvidia.com/gpu: 1" for some and smaller for others; CA binpacking calc might think there's no single node with contiguous free full GPU.

```
I0323 12:34:56 autoscaler.go:XXX] ScaleUp: unremovable pod: small-preproc-xyz - needs 0.25 gpu, but node annotation gpu-count: 1 and allocatable=1
I0323 12:34:56 autoscaler.go:XXX] No scale up: insufficient resources for full GPU allocation
```

davinder: TL;DR: fragmentation. Small pods requesting fractional shares are blocking full-GPU pods because our scheduler/device plugin treats a GPU as indivisible for scheduling decisions. We also have kube-scheduler predicate that requires nvidia.com/gpu >= request but ceil semantics vary.
lee: can we repro with a minimal Pod spec? share one please.
samir: repro below — this small job requests 0.25 GPU and stays Pending alongside a 1 GPU job.

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: small-preproc
spec:
  containers:
  - name: preproc
    image: alpine
    resources:
      requests:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
```

maria: ah — our old admission webhook that normalized GPU requests to integers was accidentally disabled in that pool. So fractional values passed through to device plugin and scheduler. The device plugin advertises a total allocatable of 4.0 GPUs, but the scheduler's scoring plugins assume integer units; mixed semantics cause CA and scheduler to disagree.
anya: ops question — what's the impact on autoscaler cost? Are we creating more nodes than necessary or starving workloads?
samir: currently starving: full-GPU jobs Pending for ~15min, CA hasn't scaled because it thinks there isn't enough demand for an extra full node under current binpack calc. If CA did scale, we'd pay for extra nodes. Longer-term we either want integer-only requests or a proper fractional-aware scheduler+plugin.
davinder: options:
- re-enable admission webhook to normalize fractional to 1 (safe, but wastes GPU for small jobs)
- enforce integer-only via a validating webhook and migrate small jobs to CPU-based preprocessing or batch them
- switch to a proper fractional device plugin + scheduler extender that supports packing shares and preemption across slices
- change CA scaling policy to be more responsive (lower scale-up delay) for GPU pools so mismatch yields quick scale-up instead of starvation

lee: can we patch validating webhook now to reject non-integer values? quick fix.
maria: yes, I can flip it in eu-west-1 dedicated-gpu pool. But need a rollout plan — there are a few repos with legitimate fractional annotations (internal testing). I'll add a whitelist for namespaces: infra-test, perf-experiments.
anya: also propose adding a kube-scheduler predicate that checks for contiguous GPU capacity (ceil semantics) so pods requesting integer GPUs still schedule correctly even when small shares exist.
davinder: +1. Also add a nightly job to scan for pods requesting <1 gpu and create a report. We had 32 small-preproc pods last week.
samir: infra-bot can you create a ticket and run a quick grep across clusters for fractional requests?
infra-bot: Created issue INFRA-7823: "fractional gpu requests passed through in eu-west-1 dedicated-gpu" assigned to @maria and @davinder. Running scan now... (results in ~2m)

(2m later)
infra-bot: Scan complete: Found 129 pods across clusters requesting nvidia.com/gpu < 1 in the last 24h. eu-west-1 dedicated-gpu: 38 pods. Summary attached to INFRA-7823.

maria: I'll schedule a short mitigation: re-enable webhook + add whitelist + a small CA policy tweak (reduce scale-up cooldown from 5m -> 90s for that nodepool). Will monitor tokenized cost impact.
lee: when you flip webhook, let's post in #deployments and coordinate a k8s API restart window if needed.
anya: follow-up: once stable, file RFC for longer-term fractional GPU sharing support or migrating tiny jobs to CPU. We should also update onboarding docs to say "no fractional GPU requests in prod".
samir: thanks all. I'll re-run example repro after webhook flip and report back here with timing and whether CA scales.

maria: flipping webhook in 10.
lee: :thumbsup:

(20m later)
maria: webhook re-enabled + CA cooldown lowered. small-preproc pods either got re-scheduled onto shared batch nodes or failed validation if in prod namespaces. Full-GPU jobs are now scheduling. Monitoring CPU and cost for next 2 hours.

samir: confirmed — a 1-GPU training job moved from Pending -> Running at 1839004380. Good catch everyone.
lee: great remediation. Follow-up RFC can propose adding a fractional-aware scheduler extender if we want real sharing.
anya: adding RFC to backlog labelled infra/scheduling.
maria: closing INFRA-7823 when RFC exists."
